  validation): the trap held the low model and cost the medium model nothing. Rev 1 is the one focused
  repair: the trap is kept and the order side becomes a sequence that needs a second order and two
  inferences (which order was in force on a date; an order being in force does not mean its comment period
  is open). Measured result for rev 1 pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 4 L30 (rule: "received by June 26, 2026"), L33-34 and L39 (portal only, all comments
  electronic). Doc 5 L25-27 (June 21 order: in effect from June 21, to run through July 21; comments "on or
  before July 10, 2026"). Doc 6 L25-27 (next order: in effect July 13 through August 12; comments "on or
  before July 31, 2026"). Six groups: rule letters, 30, not accepted; rule portal on June 25, 18, accepted;
  order comments on July 10, 22, last day of the June order's period, accepted; July 12, 22, June order
  still the one in force, period closed, not accepted; July 30, 22, July order in force, before July 31,
  accepted; August 5, 22, July order in force, period closed, not accepted. 18 + 22 + 22 = 62.
- Universe: the six groups, 136 comments in all (30 + 18 + 22 x 4); 62 accepted, 74 not (30 + 22 + 22).
- Necessity: Doc 4 is the only document with the rule's portal-only method and June 26 date. Doc 5 is the
  only document with the June order's deadline (July 10); Doc 6 and Doc 7 describe that order only as having
  "a 15-day comment period", which from June 21 gives July 6 and would drop the July 10 group (40). Doc 6
  is the only document with the July order's deadline (July 31); Doc 7 again gives only "a 15-day comment
  period" from July 13, which gives July 28 and would drop the July 30 group (40). Doc 7 is not needed:
  August 5 falls inside the July order's printed term and after its printed deadline. The wording states no
  rule, no deadline and no order date.
- Selected-lever checks (Python, 2026-10-10): gold 18 + 22 + 22 = 62. Orders' mail rule carried to the rule:
  92. An order in force taken as open for comment (July 12 and August 5 counted): 106; with the letters as
  well: 136. One of the two closed-period groups counted: 84. Label deadlines (15 days after June 21 and
  after July 13) instead of the printed ones: 18. July 30 judged against the June order's deadline: 40. Every
  route has its own value.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope, misapplies a rule or premise) -> 92, the
  orders' mail rule applied to the interim rule. Measured on rev 0 Run 1: all five low attempts counted the
  30 letters (answer 91 there; low attempt 1 wrote "Allowed methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal or mail" for
  the rule, and another gave it the EOIR rule's postmark wording). Considered and not declared, no attempt
  observed yet: an order in force taken as open for comment (106; a period that should be left out, perhaps
  "Out-of-range period", definition not saved) and the 15-day label (18). Re-declare from rev 1's observed
  wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: Python 2026-10-10: 18 + 22 = 40; 40 + 22 = 62; 30 + 18 + 4 x 22 = 136. Date
  tests: June 25 <= June 26; June 21 <= July 10 <= July 10; July 10 < July 12 < July 13; July 21 < July 30
  <= July 31; July 31 < August 5 < August 12.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 62 or the scenario's counts as comment tallies (the real
  tallies are three, five and none). Shortest route: read the DATES and ADDRESSES of the rule and the DATES
  and term of the two orders, place each date under the order then in force, add what qualifies.
- Precision/readings: "its Ebola entry order then in force" on a date is the order whose printed term
  covers that date. July 10 and July 12: only the June 21 order (the next took effect at 5:00 p.m. on
  July 13). July 30 and August 5: only the July 13 order (the June order's term ended July 21; the August
  order took effect August 12). No date falls in July 13-21, when both printed terms overlap. A comment
  received after an order's printed deadline does not meet its timing requirement even though the order
  is still in effect; nothing in the notices extends a comment period. "On or before July 10" includes
  July 10. "Letters" are mailed paper comments; the rule lists one method and requires electronic
  submission. Labelling instructions are outside "method and timing".
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md coverage lines).

sections.question: On June 25, 2026, CDC received 30 letters and 18 portal comments on its interim quarantine rule. On each of July 10, July 12, July 30 and August 5 it received 22 portal comments on its Ebola entry order then in force. How many met CDC's requirements on method and timing?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 4, DATES and ADDRESSES): comments on the interim final rule must be received by June 26, 2026. They may be submitted by one method only, the Federal eRulemaking Portal, and all comments must be submitted electronically.

Step 2. Application (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the 30 letters on the rule were not submitted electronically, so they do not meet the rule's method requirement. The 18 portal comments on the rule arrived on June 25, before June 26, and count.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, SUMMARY and DATES): the order issued on June 21, 2026 took effect that day and was to remain in effect through July 21, 2026. Written comments on it must be received on or before July 10, 2026.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 6, SUMMARY and DATES): the next order took effect on July 13, 2026 and remains in effect through August 12, 2026. Written comments on it must be received on or before July 31, 2026.

Step 5. Application (Doc 5 and Doc 6): on July 10 and on July 12 the order in force was the June 21 order, because the next order did not take effect until July 13. The 22 comments of July 10 arrived on that order's last day for comments and count. The 22 comments of July 12 arrived after it and do not count.

Step 6. Application (Doc 5 and Doc 6): on July 30 and on August 5 the order in force was the July 13 order, the June 21 order having ended on July 21. The 22 comments of July 30 arrived before July 31 and count. The 22 comments of August 5 arrived after July 31 and do not count.

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the rule's timely portal comments plus the July 10 comments on the order: 18 + 22 = 40.

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): adding the July 30 comments on the order: 40 + 22 = 62.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Wrong jurisdiction or scope: Doc 5's and Doc 6's orders accept mailed comments, but Doc 4's interim rule takes comments only through the portal. Carrying the orders' mail rule to the rule counts its 30 letters: 92. The rule's own terms give 62.
